notes.title: Gramática — ser y estar
notes.html:
Ser vs. estar

Ser for what something is: identity, origin, time, material.

Estar for how or where something is: location, condition, ongoing action.

El niño es alto. El niño está cansado.

Trampas

  1. "Estar" for location of people and things, "ser" for events: la fiesta es en mi casa.

  2. Adjectives that change meaning: aburrido (boring / bored), listo (clever / ready).

Lista de práctica en Frases para repasar.

notes.title: Podcast — Hidden Brain, habits
notes.html:
Episode on habit formation. Three takeaways:

  1. Cues beat willpower. Change the environment, not the intention.

  2. Stack a new habit onto an existing one.

  3. Missing once is fine; missing twice starts a new habit.

Episode page: hiddenbrain.org
